ledger.x: c. 2055 BC: Mentuhotep II takes the Theban throne and the Middle Kingdom begins. 'The struggle was to be concluded by Mentuhotep II, who ascended the Theban throne in 2055 BC'; infobox 'c. 2055 BC to c. 1650 BC', capital Thebes. The page names the throne, not the land.

c. 2055 BC: Mentuhotep II's war against Heracleopolis. The First Intermediate Period page dates no campaign of his; the start is set at his accession. Intef III had already moved 'into Middle Egypt against the Heracleopolitan kings'.

c. 2033 BC: Mentuhotep II conquers the north and reunites Egypt. 'would eventually defeat the Heracleopolitan kings around 2033 BC and unify the country. This event marked the beginning of the Middle Kingdom of Egypt.'
c. 2033 BC: the Heracleopolitan war ends in the Theban victory.

c. 1991 BC: Amenemhat I founds the Twelfth Dynasty. Infobox 'established c. 1991 BC'; first ruler 'Amenemhat I (c. 1991 - c. 1962 BC)'. Page: Amenemhat I 'strengthened defenses between Egypt and Asia, building the Walls of the Ruler in the East Delta region'.
c. 1991 BC: the capital moves from Thebes to Itjtawy. Page: Amenemhat I 'moved its capital to a new city named Amenemhat-itj-tawy'; no year given, set at his accession (c. 1991 BC).

c. 1944 BC: Senusret I pushes the frontier to the Second Cataract and makes Lower Nubia an Egyptian colony. 'Under his rule, Egyptian armies pushed south into Nubia as far as the Second Cataract, building a border fort at Buhen.' The page gives no year: placed at the middle of his reign (c. 1962 - c. 1926 BC, Twelfth…

c. 1873 BC: Senusret III begins his Nubian campaigns. 'He used this to launch a series of brutal campaigns in Nubia in his sixth, eighth, tenth, and sixteenth years.' Reign c. 1878 - c. 1839 BC puts year 6 at c. 1873, 8 at 1871, 10 at 1869, 16 at 1863.

c. 1863 BC: after his sixteenth-year campaign Senusret III fixes the frontier at Semna. Page: 'to establish the formal boundary between Egyptian conquests and unconquered Nubia at Semna'; the boundary has no year of its own, set at the last campaign year.

c. 1839 BC: the Sinai mining camps are run on a semi-permanent basis under Amenemhat III (c. 1839 - c. 1814 BC). The page gives no year; placed at the start of his reign. The camps are not named, so the Sinai part of Cliopatria's shape is a researcher's reading.
c. 1800 BC: the desert hinterland joins the drawn kingdom. The page is silent on the oases and deserts; the date is the year of Cliopatria's larger shape and nothing else supports it.

c. 1700 BC: a Delta kingdom, the Fourteenth Dynasty, breaks away at Avaris. The Hyksos page dates Sobekhotep IV's death 'around 1725 BC', after which 'Egypt splintered'; the page's 14th Dynasty borders (Athribis to Bubastis) are undated, so the eastern Delta is the researcher's reading. The Middle Kingdom page ends…

c. 1650 BC: the Hyksos take Memphis and Lower Egypt from the Thirteenth Dynasty. Fifteenth Dynasty page: the dynasty 'expanded to occupy Memphis' leading to the fall of the Thirteenth Dynasty there; the Hyksos date from 'Established 1650 BC'.

c. 1650 BC: Thebes passes to the Sixteenth Dynasty. 'The 16th Dynasty (c. 1650-1580 BC) ruled the Theban region in Upper Egypt'; Thebes c. 1677-1600 BC for the 13th, 16th and 17th Dynasties. The radius is the researcher's.
c. 1650 BC: Lower Nubia is lost to Kush. Second Intermediate Period page: the 13th Dynasty withdrew from the southern forts and Kush reoccupied them; placed at the Middle Kingdom's end.

c. 1650 BC: the Middle Kingdom ends and the Second Intermediate Period begins. wars.name: Reunification of Egypt under Mentuhotep II
wars.outcome: Mentuhotep II 'would eventually defeat the Heracleopolitan kings around 2033 BC and unify the country'.

wars.name: Nubian campaigns of Senusret I
wars.outcome: Lower Nubia incorporated 'as an Egyptian colony' with a border fort at Buhen.

wars.name: Nubian campaigns of Senusret III
wars.outcome: Campaigns in his 6th, 8th, 10th and 16th years ended with the formal boundary at Semna between Egyptian conquests and unconquered Nubia.

wars.name: Middle Kingdom campaigns into Canaan
wars.outcome: No territorial result: Amenemhat I's armies 'campaigned ... into southern Canaan' (Twelfth Dynasty page); 'One of Senusret's soldiers records a campaign into Canaan, perhaps against Shechem' (Middle Kingdom page); Byblos kept diplomatic ties.

certainty.note: No treaty or survey lines; the valley is bounded by desert.
